found.notes: DEBT raised by a special-purpose vehicle (the LESSOR), not by Anthropic: the SPV raises debt plus equity, buys Google TPUs (co-designed with Broadcom) and leases them to Anthropic; lease payments service the notes. Per Bloomberg (via Investing.com, 2026-06-05): A1 notes $6B priced ~T+100bp, A2 notes $24B at a 5.75% coupon, B notes $4.5B at 8.5%; senior tranches rated investment grade (private ratings); Broadcom gives residual-value support covering any shortfall for A1/A2 holders if Anthropic defaults and recovered chips sell for less than owed; roughly half syndicated to outside investors (insurers incl. Apollo's Athene, banks). Arrangers: Wells Fargo (global coordinator), BNP Paribas, Citi, UBS; A2 placement agents Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley (Yahoo pricing story). The first Bloomberg report (2026-05-28/29) had about $36B with A2 at $25B; the final is about $35B. FT (2026-08-03, via The Decoder and heise) describes the vehicle as 'Compute SPV' which bought about 1M TPUs for $35B, with a Broadcom backstop of about $30B; Google separately backstops data-center leases (10 projects, 2.4 GW; up to $44B exposure, $815M recorded), which is a different instrument. Anthropic is the lessee/obligor on the lease, not the issuer of these notes. The claim label '(lessor debt; not Anthropic-issued)' is correct; it must be excluded from Anthropic's own capital raised.

found.notes: FUNDED $5.0B plus a CONDITIONAL facility of up to $20.0B. Anthropic post (2026-04-20): 'Amazon is investing $5 billion in Anthropic today, with up to an additional $20 billion in the future'; builds on the $8B previously invested; Anthropic commits more than $100B over ten years to AWS and up to 5 GW. Amazon's 10-Q Q2-26 (filed 2026-07-31) gives the legal form: the $5.0B was invested in Anthropic 'Series G nonvoting preferred stock' in Q2 2026 (equity); the 'up to $20B' is a separate financing arrangement, 'an aggregate facility not to exceed $20.0 billion' expiring 30 months after an Anthropic liquidity event such as an IPO; at inception nothing is available to draw, amounts become available as compute-delivery milestones under the amended AWS agreement are reached, and draws are in new Anthropic convertible notes (or common stock after an IPO, subject to Amazon's ownership cap). Amazon also held an option to invest up to $5.0B in future equity financings; it exercised that in Series H ($5.0B Series H nonvoting preferred), cutting the facility to $15.0B. So Q2 2026 equity funded by Amazon was $10.0B in total ($5.0B Series G + $5.0B Series H), and up to $15.0B of conditional note capacity remained at 2026-06-30. Valuation: none in the announcement; the stock was issued as Series G preferred (announced Series G terms: $350B pre / $380B post); not stated by Amazon or Anthropic for this tranche specifically.

found.notes: FUNDED $10B 'now' plus up to $30B CONTINGENT (total up to $40B), single-origin Bloomberg reporting repeated by TechCrunch, 9to5Google, The Next Web and Yahoo Finance (all 2026-04-24): '$10 billion now in cash at a $350 billion valuation' and 'another $30 billion if Anthropic hits performance targets' (targets undisclosed); plus Google Cloud capacity of 5 GW over five years (TechCrunch) and access to up to one million Ironwood TPUs (TNW). Valuation basis: Bloomberg says 'at a $350 billion valuation' without saying pre- or post-money; $350B equals the Series G PRE-money (Series G post-money was $380B), so it most likely prices the stock at the Series G price; pre_usd_m/post_usd_m are left null because the basis is not stated. Independent, unnamed corroboration from Alphabet's 10-Q Q2-26: $20.0B of 'future capital funding commitments with a private company contingent upon the achievement of specified operational and financial milestones through 2030' (accounted for as an equity derivative) versus $30B contingent at announcement, and $21.1B of Q2-2026 purchases of non-marketable securities (22,051 six-month less 906 in Q1). That pattern fits $10B in April plus about $10B more via an option in Series H, which would cut the contingent $30B to $20B (INFERENCE: Alphabet does not name Anthropic, and Anthropic's Series H post attributes only $5B of its $15B hyperscaler money to a named company, Amazon). Google's pre-existing stake was about 14%, contractually capped at 15%, non-voting (court filings, 2025; Fortune 2026-06-04).
